title: Stirling engine
object: Beta-type Stirling demonstrator with a rhombic drive, in axial section
idea: Heat flowing from hot to cold does work: the Stirling cycle
summary: A burner heats the cap, the displacer shuttles one sealed charge of air between the hot cap and the finned cooler through a 1 mm gap regenerator, and the power piston takes work from the pressure swing. A Schmidt model drives everything: the gas is shaded by the temperature of the space it is in, the P–V loop traces live, and turning the burner down shrinks the loop and slows the flywheel towards its stall.
usedFor: Thermodynamics teaching: the Stirling cycle, Schmidt analysis, Carnot and the role of the regenerator
Explaining heat engines and why a temperature difference is needed to do work
Product or museum pages for demonstrator engines and rhombic drives
views: Detail D hot joint and gap regenerator 5:1
